feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader: the experience is relevant, progressive, and supported by useful scale indicators. It reads clearly overall, but it is slightly repetitive and too dense in places, which reduces impact and makes the strongest achievements harder to spot quickly.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression at NACo strongly support leadership in digital platforms, governance, and communications systems.  
- Good credibility signals: metrics like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers” add substance and scale.  
- Broad but coherent skill set: strategy, CMS/platform work, analytics, multimedia, and AI-enabled search are presented as a logical leadership profile.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and save space for more quantified outcomes.  
- Add more results-focused bullets: several bullets describe responsibilities (“led,” “supported,” “advised”) without showing business/user impact, efficiency gains, engagement growth, or adoption outcomes.  
- Fix style consistency issues: use one name format (“Coleman Davis” vs “Coleman DAVIS”); standardize punctuation around lists and hyphenation (“organization-wide,” “front-end”). No major misspellings found, but wording like “Ranked among the top public universities…” is unnecessary and weakens precision.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning and clear seniority, but the intro is slightly generic and repeats several ideas already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with one or two concrete signals of scope or sector impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten phrasing and reduce abstraction: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years’ experience leading public-sector web platforms, governance, and content operations for high-volume communications.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct leadership language such as “leading modernization of enterprise websites, analytics ecosystems, editorial workflows, and multimedia programs.”
- Consider adding one concrete scale marker from recent experience, e.g. “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views,” if you want a more evidence-based intro.
- Refine the second sentence to: “Specializes in enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled user experiences for mission-driven organizations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects.
- “Digital leader” and “leader” in the subtitle/header feel repetitive.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align well with the headline and recent roles, but this block overlaps heavily with the summary and Topline Skills. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize strategic capability areas rather than repeating phrasing used elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, cleaner labels for scanability: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight systems • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Replace “content experiences” with “content discovery” for sharper meaning and less buzzword feel.
- Change “operations” to “leadership” where appropriate to better reflect seniority.
- Standardize style by avoiding mixed noun forms; keep all items as capability areas.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header summary and all four Topline Skills blocks.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” is close to existing “Public-sector and advocacy messaging.”
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it currently reads like a repeat of the recent freelance and NACo experience rather than a distinct closing highlight section. Tightening phrasing and standardizing style will improve scanability and impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add dates or “Selected Recent Projects” framing to reinforce recency and distinguish this from core experience.
- Use parallel, outcome-oriented phrasing: start each item with a strong verb and end with a clear purpose or result.
- Standardize style and punctuation; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for consistency and readability.
- Consider trimming to 2–3 highest-value projects, especially AI Hybrid Search and the Drupal microsite, to keep the footer concise.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with the current freelance and NACo bullets.
- The anniversary campaign may add the most unique detail because it introduces experiential/display work not emphasized elsewhere.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Website

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten it around outcomes, ownership, and 2–3 signature contributions that distinguish it from the NACo roles below.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Lead digital strategy, platform improvement, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization, with emphasis on Drupal, governance, analytics, and AI-enabled discovery.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise,” “deliver”) with ownership verbs: “Lead,” “Design,” “Build,” “Implement,” “Establish.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets and foreground impact:
- Built Drupal campaign/microsite frameworks, modular content components, and member-facing toolkits to speed campaign launches and improve reuse.
- Established cross-channel workflows, governance standards, and analytics systems to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.
- Led AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content model, and discovery UX for complex policy/member content.
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages/templates, launch speed, traffic, engagement, search success, publisher adoption, or workflow time saved.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” overlaps with Director of Digital Media; make this entry more hands-on/build-focused.
- Microsites and AI search also appear in Recent Projects/footer; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will read even better if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation wins, and avoid repeating channel-management points covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad opener with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the website transformation and outcome: “Spearheaded redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based; add growth, engagement, or send-volume metrics if available rather than “tens of thousands”/“thousands.”
- Tighten remaining bullets with action + result phrasing: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio…”; “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting stack…”; “Established governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning workflows…”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-programming language may duplicate older NACo entries unless framed here as building new organizational capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing operational leadership, cross-team coordination, and channel growth before the larger platform/governance work in 2022–2024.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to focus on scope and progression: “Directed day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy messaging.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and specific: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger line: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.” If possible, add metrics such as send volume, open rates, production cadence, or team/stakeholder count.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial planning” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning language.
- Weekly video work also overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; frame this here as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/consulting bullets. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and public-sector relevance rather than generic content terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience strategy and content planning
- Consider swapping “content planning” for a more senior term like “audience strategy” or “content operations.”
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this area to scale from recent roles (e.g., 10,000+ page web ecosystem, 50+ publishers, 3.5M annual page views) rather than listing broad capabilities only.
- Keep wording parallel: all noun phrases, no mixed styles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “governance,” and “multi-channel communications” already appear in the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; use one version consistently.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it’s too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize current, differentiating strengths tied to recent Drupal modernization and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to a capability-led line, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Lead with Drupal and CMS modernization; they’re most supported by recent experience. Move older/secondary platforms like WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages to “Technical + IT.”
- Tighten phrasing: change “Airtable systems” to “Airtable-based content systems” and “AI-enabled search experiences” to “AI-enabled search and discovery.”
- If space allows, add one impact cue: “for high-volume public-sector sites” or “for enterprise content operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages duplicate the “Technical + IT” platform list.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also echo Core Competencies almost verbatim.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it into higher-value capability language that emphasizes decision support and optimization.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Analytics infrastructure (GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI)”
- Replace weaker terms like “Leadership reporting” with stronger outcome-oriented language: “Executive dashboards and decision support”
- Tighten and group related items: “User behavior analysis (Microsoft Clarity), KPI framework design, SEO and performance optimization”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics infrastructure (GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI) • User behavior insights (Microsoft Clarity) • KPI framework design • Executive dashboards and decision support • SEO and performance optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating every tool here if the Technical + IT section already carries the full platform list.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo bullets. Make it more senior, distinctive, and tied to delivery capability rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe for scope and leadership: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio buildout and operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems • Virtual event production”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more senior phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production” to better match Director-level experience.
- Consider swapping “Hybrid and virtual event production” to “Livestream and hybrid event delivery” for stronger action and less repetition.
- If space allows, add one differentiator: “Recurring advocacy video programming” or “Studio-based multimedia operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; vary wording here or remove one.
- “Studio operations” and “PTZ camera systems” are useful, but avoid overemphasizing tactical details if targeting digital leadership roles.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Use this section to signal depth or recency, not just repeat names.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint / Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If accurate, add level/scope to the strongest platform: e.g., Drupal 9/10, enterprise publishing environments, multi-author governance.
- Consider ordering by relevance/recency: Drupal first, then SharePoint/Power Pages if current, then WordPress, GitHub Pages last.
- If space allows, replace the weakest item with a more differentiating platform note: “Drupal CMS architecture” or “SharePoint intranet publishing.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills [2]; consider trimming one version or making this one more implementation-focused.
- “GitHub Pages” may undersell seniority unless tied to a specific use case or removed.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this item reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more current and implementation-focused, emphasizing tools you actively use in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End Development & Technical Implementation
- Tighten phrasing to: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- If accurate, add level/context instead of just tools: Front-end development (HTML5/CSS3/JavaScript/jQuery) • API integrations • tag management (GTM) • edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • CI/CD automation (GitHub Actions)
- If space allows, prioritize recent relevance by dropping older/basic terms or adding one outcome-linked qualifier elsewhere in experience, e.g., “used for Drupal microsites, analytics deployment, and workflow automation”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- Consider removing either this item or the overlapping Topline Skills line to avoid repetitive skills stacking.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already highlighted elsewhere. Make it more purposeful by grouping tools by function and emphasizing systems/automation over basic collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Automation & workflow systems: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Trello
- If space allows, group by use: Automation/integration: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/workflow management: Jira, Asana, Trello
- Drop lower-signal collaboration tools unless they are central to delivery: Slack, Teams, Basecamp
- Keep only tools you’ve actively used to build workflows, not just communicate or track tasks

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same emphasis here without adding specificity
- Jira/Asana/Trello may feel interchangeable; listing all three is fine only if each reflects meaningful hands-on use

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this item is too bare and undersells a clear strength from recent roles: enterprise email operations and member communications. It should signal scale and platform ownership, not just list vendor names.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Enterprise newsletter operations • Audience segmentation
- If accurate, strengthen further with scope: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Newsletter production at scale • List segmentation • Campaign deployment
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent work; lead with the most current/enterprise-relevant system.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Engagement” is vague and overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies; use more specific email/CRM language.
- Avoid adding analytics terms here, since those are already covered well in “Data, Analytics & Optimization.”

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant stack, but this item is mostly a tool list and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Tighten it to emphasize analysis/optimization capability, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Analytics, Reporting & Optimization
- Replace with: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • KPI reporting • SEO/performance analysis • Experimentation
- Swap “A/B testing” for “Experimentation” unless you’ve directly run formal tests; it reads broader and safer.
- If space allows, prioritize the most recent/high-impact tools first: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly duplicated by “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Consider trimming one section or making this one more tool-focused and the other more outcome-focused.
- “Dashboarding” is redundant with Looker Studio/Power BI and weaker than “KPI reporting” or “performance analysis.”

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads as setup rather than impact. Tighten it to emphasize team-building, channel ownership, and concrete outputs without repeating later NACo leadership bullets.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground advancement and scope: “Promoted through two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social, and multimedia operations.”
- Add clearer outcomes if available: website refresh size/timeline, livestream/event volume, weekly video cadence, audience growth, or process improvements.
- Replace soft phrasing like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows” with specifics: “standardized publishing workflows,” “produced weekly advocacy videos,” “managed livestream production.”
- Suggested version: “Promoted through two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting daily web, email, social, and multimedia operations. Contributed to a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, standardized digital publishing workflows, and provided day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid overemphasizing weekly video updates; that is already covered in the 2018–2022 role.
- Don’t restate broad channel leadership already captured more strongly in later NACo positions.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and underplays the strongest differentiator: launching NACo’s first podcast. Since later roles already cover digital/media growth, this item should emphasize innovation/program support and the podcast as a first.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a more active, specific line: “Produced multimedia and digital content to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of episodes, audiences reached, projects coordinated, or teams/stakeholders supported.
- Keep it to 1–2 concise sentences; this is an older role, so avoid over-detail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content/multimedia” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overemphasize video or digital team-building here; those achievements belong to 2015–2024 entries.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a mixed list of software, workflows, and production capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and multiple work-experience bullets, so tighten it to tool-specific skills and keep the strongest, current capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Multimedia Tools
